title: More Than Meets the Eye: The Spectrum
objective: After this level you can explain that visible light is one small part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
summary: Radio waves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are all light, differing only in wavelength.

cards.headline: Your eyes are missing almost everything.
cards.body: Most of the light in the universe is invisible to us. Astronomers have learned to see it anyway.

cards.headline: One spectrum, many names
cards.body: Radio waves, microwaves, infrared, visible light, ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays are all the same thing: light. What makes them different is wavelength. Radio waves are the longest, gamma rays the shortest, and visible light is a thin sliver in between.

cards.headline: Same speed, every kind
cards.body: Every kind of light, from radio to gamma rays, crosses space at the speed of light. Within the visible band, the colors are wavelengths too: red is the longest and violet the shortest.

cards.fact: Human eyes see only wavelengths from about 380 to 700 nanometers.
cards.context: Anything longer, like infrared, or shorter, like ultraviolet, is invisible to us. Some animals, such as bees, can see ultraviolet.

cards.headline: Spectrum: revealed
learned: Visible light is a small part of the spectrum
Radio → gamma rays: long to short wavelengths
All light travels at the same speed
Red is the longest visible wavelength; violet the shortest

questions.prompt: What makes radio waves, visible light and X-rays different?

options.label: How fast each one travels through space
options.rationale: They all travel at the speed of light.

options.label: Which objects are able to give them off
options.rationale: The key difference is a property of the light itself.

options.label: Whether they are made of particles
options.rationale: They are all forms of light.

questions.explanation: They are all light. The difference is wavelength: radio waves are longest, gamma rays shortest.

questions.prompt: Which list goes from longest wavelength to shortest?

options.label: Gamma rays → visible light → radio waves
Visible light → radio waves → X-rays
options.rationale: Radio waves are longer than visible light.

options.label: X-rays → radio waves → gamma rays
options.rationale: Radio waves are the longest of all.

questions.explanation: Radio waves are the longest, visible light sits in the middle, and X-rays (then gamma rays) are the shortest.

questions.prompt: From Level 8: light-years are based on the speed of light. Does a light-year mean the same distance for radio waves?

options.label: Yes: every kind of light travels at the same speed
No: radio waves are much slower than visible light
options.rationale: All light travels at the same speed.

options.label: No: only visible light counts as real light
Only for radio waves from nearby stars
options.rationale: The speed doesn’t depend on the source.

questions.explanation: All electromagnetic radiation travels at the speed of light, so a light-year is the same distance whichever kind of light you measure with.
